lecture_title: Spin, Measurement, and the Two-Dimensional State Space

assets.name: lecture_02_figure_02.png
assets.rationale: This is the first frame in which the arrow is fully drawn and clearly legible on a clean portion of the board. The earlier candidates are blank or still in the middle of the stroke, while the later frame adds more lecturer presence without improving the visible notation.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: I'll draw it as a little arrow.

assets.name: lecture_02_figure_03.png
assets.rationale: This frame gives the cleanest overall board state among the four nearly identical candidates. Both visible equations are fully legible, the horizontal arrow with the x label is still present at the left edge, and Susskind is not blocking the notation. It is the most useful combined record of the symbolic labels and the axis orientation cue.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: get sigma x equals minus one,

assets.name: lecture_02_figure_04.png
assets.rationale: This frame gives the best balance of completeness and clarity. The main equation \(\langle \sigma_m \rangle = n\cdot m\) is fully legible, \(\sigma_x=\pm1\) remains visible above it, and Susskind is not blocking the writing. Earlier and later frames are very similar, but this one preserves slightly more of both the left-side mathematics and the adjacent board context without cropping the key equation.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: at one point you were drawing a spin

assets.name: lecture_02_figure_05.png
assets.rationale: The completed board state shows a linear combination, scalar multiplication, and the conjugate-reversal rule for the inner product without the lecturer obscuring the formulas.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: The inner product is a complex number, and it satisfies that it is equal to the complex conjugate of the opposite order.
assets.caption_hint: linear combinations and conjugate-symmetric inner product

assets.name: lecture_02_figure_06.png
assets.rationale: The lecturer has stepped away from a complete board state containing the general up-down expansion, the summed Born probabilities, and the equivalent unit-norm condition.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: The inner product of A with itself is equal to one.

assets.name: lecture_02_figure_07.png
assets.rationale: This completed board state cleanly shows the right and left states as equal-weight up-down combinations, their column vectors, and their zero overlap.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: This tells us that right and left are orthogonal to each other.

assets.name: lecture_02_figure_08.png
assets.rationale: All six column vectors are visible at once, with the lecturer outside the mathematical content and the relative imaginary signs legible.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: We take this times the complex conjugate of this plus this times the complex conjugate of this.
assets.caption_hint: six spin states in the up-down basis

assets.name: lecture_02_figure_09.png
assets.rationale: The frame preserves the finished in-state expansion in the right-left basis and the modulus-squared calculation giving one half.
assets.subtitle_excerpt: The magnitude of this is one over square root of two and so is the magnitude of this.
assets.caption_hint: in-state change of basis and equal probabilities
